before: Source tracing found tuple-only signed-record matching followed by live probe and dispatch through caller-supplied endpoints, which could omit endorsed pins.
after: Core pin-consensus tests and a Linux loopback no-dispatch regression show endorsed pins retained through selection; Linux explicit pins fail closed before outbound I/O.
review: Independent source reviewer identified the pin loss; separate Core and Linux owners fixed their paths.
limitation: No original-source adversarial TLS listener was run, so the finding remains needs_validation for demonstrated network impact.

before: Isolated original Core source accepted a one-of-two signed coordinator listing for claim, incoming delivery, and outgoing forward; Linux source merged directory records before member admission.
after: Patched local signed fixtures reject one-of-two and accept two-of-two with distinct signing keys; valid live peers remain admitted. Final package suite results are in the owner report.
review: The parent traced both implementations; independent skill_forward_test reviewer challenged signer provenance and mirror fallback. Core and Linux repairs had separate owners.
limitation: The Linux outgoing curated route shares the tested membership helper but has no separate end-to-end forwarding fixture.

before: Forged self-signed source advertising an allowed tuple reached route storage; isolated original Core source failed authentication-rejection assertion.
after: Patched tests reject forged key, accept a real live peer with a dummy send capability, and try another allowed endpoint when the first has the wrong identity or is unavailable.
review: Parent and independent reviewer challenged endpoint binding, pin consumption, and alternate endpoint behavior; Core and Linux fixes were implemented separately.
limitation: Linux outbound URLSession transport cannot verify an explicit TLS leaf fingerprint and now rejects such configured outbound endpoints before I/O.

before: The original existing-channel loopback fixture reached route storage after the operator allowlist was emptied.
after: The same fixture rejects the revoked peer before storage; the handler also checks policy after asynchronous admission before incoming append and outgoing send.
review: Parent independently identified and traced the constructor/live-policy mismatch; relay_core authored and tested the fix.
limitation: The regression revokes before sending the next request; it does not force a policy update during an in-flight network fetch.

before: Manual Linux claim returned success and stored dummy outsider ownership; isolated original Core solo test failed rejection and empty-ledger assertions. Both snapshot read paths could assign directory peers.
after: Outsider claims reject, live manual host and standard peers succeed, curated quorum applies, and snapshot reads do not import peers. Existing owners remain in snapshots while offline.
review: Parent traced all ledger writers and reviewed the fixes; independent skill_forward_test reviewer identified read-side import and multi-endpoint compatibility.
limitation: Open mode remains permissionless by design; historical persisted claims are not auto reassigned.

before: An original-code test changing only operatorNote failed four assertions because form round-tripping stripped configured endpoint trust fields.
after: The same focused regression passes after merging matching current endpoint anchors, including case-insensitive hostname matching.
review: Independent reviewer traced the lossy form serializer; relay owner reproduced and repaired the effect.
limitation: Anchors for a genuinely new endpoint still must come from startup configuration, because the URL-only form does not expose anchor editing.

before: Wrong-federation first .info persisted a dummy directory key; a concurrent store regression allowed a different key to replace an existing pin.
after: The handler checks coordinator identity and valid signed snapshot before new pinning; a configured directory key is honored; the store pins by atomic compare-or-set and rejects replacement.
review: Parent challenged first-contact and configured-key paths; relay_core reproduced the original effects and tested the repair.
limitation: A first contact without configured key on unauthenticated transport retains TOFU exposure; existing pins require operator inspection.
